migration.description: Add durable single-installation deployment candidates, slots, operations, audit events, idempotency keys and installation roles.
migration.release_unit_description: Deployment control plane foundation for immutable candidates and blue-green promotion.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds deployment-control state and installation roles without changing existing project, execution or Connector rows. Older Server and Worker candidates ignore the additive tables; deployment-capable candidates require the migration before exposing the control surface.

durable_state.description: One installation row, immutable candidate identities, two slot rows, durable operation intent/result rows, append-only deployment events, idempotency request hashes and installation-level deployment roles.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL tables managed by the embedded Goose migration history; no existing row rewrite or down-migration is used by the program.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Phase-one candidates before deployment control migration 00017
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one candidates containing deployment control migration 00017
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Earlier candidates do not read deployment tables. Deployment-capable candidates require the additive schema and use only forward-compatible state transitions.

ordered_operations.description: Create deployment installation, candidate, slot, operation, event, idempotency and role tables with fail-closed enum checks.

rollout_signals: Goose records migration 00017 before the deployment controller reports ready.
The controller exposes no deployment write capability until the installation state and role tables are queryable.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version-or-switchback-only-when-the-current candidate can read the deployment rows

validation: Empty-database startup applies migration 00017 idempotently before controller readiness.
Repeated idempotency keys with the same request hash return the original operation and a changed hash fails closed.
A stale expected-current fingerprint cannot start a mutating operation.
Unknown operations remain observable and can be reconciled without creating a second side effect.
